title: Wake up your hands
description: Sit at the center, drop your shoulders, and rest five fingers. You do not need a song yet.
intro: This is the hello, not the piece. If your body is comfortable, whatever you play next comes out easier.

steps.title: Sit at the center
steps.say: Find the C that sits right in front of your navel. Bring the bench in until your elbows rest a little in front of your body, loose.
steps.tip: Both feet touch the floor. If your shoulders climb toward your ears, drop them before you go on.
steps.cheer: That is your spot. Playing is easier from here.

steps.title: Shake and let go
steps.say: Let your hands fall to your sides and shake them, as if you were drying water. Three times. Then rest them on your lap for a second.
steps.tip: Soft wrists matter more than speed. If they feel stiff, shake again.
steps.cheer: Light hands. They stay that way.

steps.title: Land the right hand
steps.say: Thumb on C. The other fingers, in order, on D, E, F, and G. Do not press the keys down: only the weight of the hand, as if the keyboard were a warm table.
steps.tip: One finger per key. The elbow stays close to the body, without opening the wing.
steps.cheer: Five fingers, five keys. They have a map now.

steps.title: Wave with each finger
steps.say: Without changing keys, lift and lower one finger at a time: thumb, index, middle, ring, and pinky. The others stay still.
steps.tip: If one finger drags its neighbor, stay with that finger only. One slow pass is enough.
steps.cheer: Each finger already knows its key.

steps.title: Now the left hand
steps.say: Move down one octave. The pinky goes on C and, toward the right, D, E, F, and G with the thumb. Rest them, then lift one finger at a time again.
steps.tip: The left hand feels odd at first. It is the first time: one pass is enough.

title: The little path from C
description: Five notes up and back, very slowly. The first sound of the day, with no song and no rush.
intro: One clean pass is worth several fast ones. Say “one” out loud every time a note sounds.

steps.title: A piano and a one
steps.say: Choose a piano tone. Say “one” out loud, calmly. That one is today’s pulse: every note lands on it.
steps.tip: If you prefer the CT-X800 metronome, leave it near 60. Your voice works too.
steps.cheer: You have a pulse. The notes walk on that one.

steps.title: Climb with the right hand
steps.say: Thumb on C. Play C, D, E, F, G. One note for each one. Release the key before you play the next.
steps.tip: If two keys sound at once, the finger was lying flat. Lift it a little and start again on C.
steps.cheer: You climbed the stairs. Five steps.

steps.title: Come back the same way
steps.say: From G, return: G, F, E, D, C. The pinky starts and the thumb closes on C. Same one, same calm.
steps.tip: The final C can last a little longer. It is the period.
steps.cheer: There and back. That is already a phrase.

steps.title: The left hand copies the path
steps.say: Pinky on the lower C. Climb C, D, E, F, G and come back down. The thumb is the one that reaches G.
steps.tip: Slower than the right hand. If a finger sticks, stop and wave with that finger only.
steps.cheer: The left hand knows the path.
steps.action: The left hand made the trip

steps.title: One softer pass
steps.say: Pick a hand, whichever you want. Repeat the whole path more softly, as if the keys were warm. One pass only.
steps.tip: If it feels heavy, do not repeat it ten times. Tomorrow this same pass will be easier.
steps.cheer: Round done. You can open a song now.
